literal: Having been born in a noble family, him who is ashamed of blame in himself, even by giving, securing friendship is necessary.
translation: One must secure the friendship of a person born of noble lineage who shrinks from disgrace, even if one has to give up something of value to obtain it.
modern: நல்ல குடியில் பிறந்து, தன் மேல் பழி வருவதற்கு நாணுகின்ற ஒருவனுடைய நட்பை, ஏதேனும் கொடுத்தாவது நாம் பெற்றுக்கொள்ள வேண்டும்.
explanation: This couplet outlines the essential qualities of an ideal friend and the lengths to which one should go to secure their companionship. The poet identifies two key traits: being born into a family of good values (குடிப்பிறந்து) and possessing a deep-seated dread of disgrace or wrongdoing (பழிநாணுவான்). A person who fears blame will naturally act with integrity and loyalty. The phrase 'கொடுத்தும் கொளல்வேண்டும்' emphasizes that such a virtuous friend is so rare and valuable that one should be willing to sacrifice material wealth or other resources just to win their friendship.
